title: Finite good refinement of a Noetherian locally closed partition
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space whose closed subsets satisfy the descending-chain condition. Let $T=\coprod_{a\in A}P_a$ be a finite partition into locally closed subsets [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. Then there is a finite partition $T=\coprod_{b\in B}Q_b$ into nonempty locally closed subsets, each $Q_b$ contained in some $P_a$, such that for all $b,c\in B$ one has $Q_b\cap\overline{Q_c}\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow Q_b\subseteq\overline{Q_c}$. Thus each $\overline{Q_c}$ is a union of members of this partition; this property is called a good stratification. If $T=\varnothing$, the empty partition is allowed.

proof.text: Prove simultaneously for every closed subset $F\subseteq T$ and every finite locally closed partition of $F$ that the asserted finite good refinement exists in $F$. The descending-chain condition gives induction on strict inclusion of closed subsets: a nonempty family with no minimal member would, by choosing a strictly smaller member repeatedly, produce a strictly descending infinite chain. Closed subsets of a closed $F$ are closed in $T$, so the same condition holds in $F$. The empty space has the empty refinement. At a nonempty $F$, assume the assertion for all proper closed subsets of $F$; for the remaining steps rename $F$ as $T$.

By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] and [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], write $T=Z_1\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$ as the finite union of its distinct irreducible components, with $r\geq1$. These are nonempty, irreducible, closed and maximal by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. The Noetherian hypothesis in the finite-components statement is satisfied by the minimal-element argument of step 1.

Fix $Z=Z_1$ and put $O=T\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne1}Z_j$. This is open and contained in $Z$. It is nonempty: otherwise irreducibility would imply that $Z$ is contained in one of the other finitely many components (apply the closed two-set condition repeatedly), contrary to maximality and distinctness. Since $T=\bigcup_a\overline{P_a}$, the same finite closed-cover argument gives an $a$ with $Z\subseteq\overline{P_a}$. By [def-weil-locally-closed-subset], write $P_a=V\cap D$ with $V$ open and $D$ closed; then $Z\subseteq D$. The nonempty open $O$ meets $P_a$, because it contains a point of $Z\subseteq\overline{P_a}$. Consequently $U=O\cap V=O\cap P_a$ is a nonempty open subset of $T$ contained in $P_a$. This derives precisely the open subset used in Tag 09Y5 without assuming that $T$ is a scheme.

Set $C=T\setminus U$ and $H=\overline U\setminus U=C\cap\overline U$. For every original part form $R_a^1=P_a\cap C\cap\overline U$ and $R_a^2=P_a\cap C\cap(T\setminus\overline U)$, deleting empty sets. These form a finite disjoint partition of $C$, refining the original parts, and $H=\bigcup_aR_a^1$. They are locally closed by [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]: if $P_a=V_a\cap D_a$, the first is $V_a\cap(D_a\cap C\cap\overline U)$ and the second is $(V_a\cap(T\setminus\overline U))\cap(D_a\cap C)$. Thus this is a partition to which the induction hypothesis applies on the proper closed subset $C\subsetneq T$.

Obtain by induction a finite good partition $C=\coprod_b Q_b$ refining the $R_a^k$, with all $Q_b$ nonempty. Each $Q_b$ is locally closed in $T$ as well: an open of $C$ is $C\cap V_b$ with $V_b$ open in $T$, and a closed subset of the closed subspace $C$ is closed in $T$, so the expression open intersect closed from [def-weil-locally-closed-subset] gives the claim. For any $Q_b\subseteq C$, its closure in $T$ is contained in $C$ and equals its closure in $C$, by the defining minimality of closure. The induction hypothesis therefore gives goodness for every pair of these strata with closures taken in $T$.

Adjoin $U$ to the $Q_b$. This is a finite partition of $T$ into nonempty locally closed parts refining the $P_a$. For a pair with source part $U$ and target part $Q_b$, the intersection $U\cap\overline{Q_b}$ is empty since $\overline{Q_b}\subseteq C$. For a pair with source $Q_b$ and target $U$, refinement in step 4 places $Q_b$ either inside $H\subseteq\overline U$ or inside $T\setminus\overline U$; hence intersection with $\overline U$ implies containment. The pair $(U,U)$ satisfies containment automatically. Together with step 5 these are all pairs, proving goodness. Finally, every point of $\overline Q$ lies in a unique part of the partition, and goodness puts that whole part inside $\overline Q$. Thus each stratum closure is a union of parts, as asserted. This completes the induction.
